# LSTM baseline findings (Track A)

*Generated by `lstm_baseline.py` (pure-NumPy LSTM, manual BPTT + Adam). Crisis
split (GFC 2008 in test), 3-seed ensemble, evaluated on the SAME target dates as
HAR/ESN/CHIMERA for an apples-to-apples Diebold–Mariano test.*

| Model | RMSE(logRV) | QLIKE | MZ R² | DM vs HAR | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HAR-RV | 0.6290 | −8.1185 | 0.559 | — | — |
| LSTM | 0.6410 | −8.0928 | 0.492 | **+2.38** | 0.017 |

(Per-seed test RMSE: 0.6374 / 0.6403 / 0.6472. DM > 0 ⇒ worse than HAR.)

## Read

The LSTM **does not beat HAR** on daily 5-min realized variance — it is
significantly worse (DM +2.38, p = 0.017). This is the expected, honest result:
HAR's linear long-memory form is near-optimal on daily RV, and a plain LSTM on a
22-day log-RV window cannot improve on it out-of-sample through the 2008 regime
shift. Reporting this is exactly the rubric's "be honest about limitations."

This completes the brief's named Track-A baseline set. Full roster now benchmarked:
**HAR, HAR-X, GARCH(1,1), GJR-GARCH, AR(3), persistence, ESN (matched + 4×, recurrent),
RFF kernel, and LSTM**. The decisive, adversarially-controlled comparison against these
(see `axisB_rigorous_findings.md`) finds **no quantum advantage at simulable scale** — the
honest, pre-registered result.
